h: Giving Thanks for the Four Redemptions of Shabbos

p: the four who must give thanks,
מֵהַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
by the Baal Shem Tov, may the memory of the tzaddik be a blessing.
that all the corruptions in the world
came about from the first sin,
and the subjugation by the kingdoms.
And when the holiness of Shabbos enters,
a repair is made for these blemishes.
And therefore we say the psalm
And this is "whom He redeemed from the hand of the oppressor":
against the oppressor who oppresses you"
who oppresses the heart of Yisrael,
And "from the lands He gathered them"
alludes to the subjugation by the kingdoms.
redemption takes place on holy Shabbos.
And after this are mentioned in detail
that is, those who travel through deserts;
and it alludes to the souls
through the leaven in the dough,
which puts laziness into the heart,
so that one goes idle from words of Torah;
and their soul longs for holiness;
only he has nothing with which
because of laziness in words of Torah.
And when the holiness of Shabbos arrives,
"let them thank Hashem for His kindness,
for He has satisfied the longing soul":
there is satisfaction for his thirst;
"and the hungry soul He has filled with good,"
וְאֵין טוֹב אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה (אָבוֹת ו, ג)
"Those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death":
these are those who sit in prison,
the subjugation by the kingdoms in general,
in the hands of a foreign subjugation;
and likewise, in detail, in the soul:
all kinds of pain and hardship
on account of the yoke of livelihood
all the days of the week,
that bring darkness into the soul,
so that one cannot attain holiness;
"let them thank Hashem for His kindness,
for He has broken the doors of copper":
for there is release and redemption
And after this are specified as well
namely, a sick person who was healed.
just as there are illnesses of the body,
so there are illnesses of the soul;
is on account of the leaven in the dough,
which are food for the soul
and they reach the gates of death";
for the wicked in their lifetime are called dead (Berachos 18b).
that is, the holiness of Shabbos,
and rescues them from their pits":
"Those who go down to the sea":
this refers to the actual subjugation by the kingdoms,
they roar like the roaring of the seas";
"He stills the roaring of the seas,
the roaring of their waves, and the tumult of the nations."
For all the deficiencies and blemishes
cling also to the souls of Yisrael;
and with the holiness of Shabbos
